docs.title: Add an Embedding Method
docs.text:
1. Create method file in ragbench/embedding/methods/:
# embedding/methods/my_embedder.py
from typing import List
from ragbench.embedding.base import BaseEmbedder

class MyEmbedder(BaseEmbedder):
    """My custom embedder."""

    def __init__(self, model: str = "default", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.model = model
        # Initialize your model here

    def embed_texts(self, texts: List[str]) -> List[List[float]]:
        """Embed texts and return vectors."""
        # Your embedding logic here
        return embeddings

    @classmethod
    def is_available(cls) -> bool:
        """Check if dependencies are installed."""
        try:
            import my_package
            return True
        except ImportError:
            return False
  1. Register the method in embedding/__init__.py:
REGISTRY.register(
    name="my_embedder",
    class_ref=MyEmbedder,
    category="custom",
    tags=["local", "fast"],
    description="My custom embedding method"
)
  1. Write tests in tests/test_embedding_methods.py:
def test_my_embedder():
    embedder = Embedder("my_embedder")
    vectors = embedder.embed(["hello", "world"])
    assert len(vectors) == 2
    assert len(vectors[0].vector) > 0
  1. Update documentation in docs/layers/03-embedding.md

docs.text: For detailed architecture information, see the Comprehensive Guide - Part 1.

docs.title: Quick Overview
docs.text:
RAGBench is built on a 7-layer architecture where each layer is completely independent and communicates through well-defined data contracts:

Layer 1: Ingestion (82 connectors) → Document
Layer 2: Chunking (106 methods) → Chunk  
Layer 3: Embedding (62 methods) → EmbeddedChunk
Layer 4: Vector Stores (41 stores) → Storage
Layer 5: Retrieval (28 methods) → RetrievalResult
Layer 6: Reranking (21 methods) → Reranked Results
Layer 7: Generation (9 providers) → Answer

docs.title: 1. Layer Independence
docs.text: Each layer can be used standalone without requiring other layers. No circular dependencies exist.

docs.title: 2. Data Contracts
docs.text: Layers communicate through immutable data classes: - Document: Raw content from ingestion - Chunk: Split pieces with metadata - EmbeddedChunk: Chunks with vector embeddings - RetrievalResult: Retrieved chunks with scores - GeneratedAnswer: Final answer with sources

docs.title: 3. Registry Pattern
docs.text:
Every layer uses a registry for method discovery: 

from ragbench.embedding import REGISTRY

# List all methods
REGISTRY.list_names()

# Get method info
REGISTRY.get_info("openai")

# Check availability
REGISTRY.is_available("bge")

docs.title: 4. Smart Auto-Routing
docs.text: When method is not specified, RAGBench automatically selects the best one based on: - Content type (text, code, image) - Query characteristics - Available resources (API keys, models) - Store capabilities

docs.title: 1.1 What is RAGBench?
docs.text:
RAGBench (formerly OmniLoad) is a layered, open-source auto-RAG framework designed for building production-ready Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It provides a complete pipeline from document ingestion to answer generation, with every layer being:

  • Independent: Each layer works standalone without dependencies on other layers
  • Connectable: Layers communicate through tiny, well-defined data contracts
  • Chainable: The entire pipeline can be executed with a single function call

docs.title: 1.1.1 What is RAG?
docs.text:
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) by:

  1. Retrieving relevant information from a knowledge base
  2. Augmenting the LLM prompt with this context
  3. Generating accurate, grounded answers based on retrieved facts

This approach solves key LLM limitations: - ❌ Hallucinations (making up facts) - ❌ Outdated knowledge (training cutoff) - ❌ No domain-specific knowledge - ❌ Cannot cite sources

RAG enables: - ✅ Factual, source-backed answers - ✅ Up-to-date information - ✅ Domain expertise - ✅ Traceable citations

docs.title: 1.1.2 Why RAGBench?
docs.text:
Problem: Most RAG frameworks are monolithic, tightly coupled, and hard to customize.

Solution: RAGBench provides:

  1. Layer Independence: Use any layer standalone or combine them
  2. Method Diversity:
  3. 82 document connectors
  4. 106 chunking methods
  5. 61 embedding methods
  6. 41 vector stores
  7. 28 retrieval methods
  8. 21 reranking methods

  9. 9 LLM providers

  10. Smart Defaults: Auto-routing picks optimal methods for your data

  11. Offline Capability: Works without API keys using local baselines
  12. Production-Ready: Robust error handling, caching, and monitoring

docs.title: 1.1.3 Core Philosophy
docs.text:
"One folder per method"

Every method (connector, chunker, embedder, etc.) lives in its own folder with: - metadata.json - Method configuration - Implementation file(s) - requirements.txt - Dependencies - __init__.py - Public API

This makes RAGBench: - Discoverable: New methods are auto-registered - Extensible: Add methods without modifying core - Maintainable: Each method is isolated - Testable: Layer independence is enforced

docs.title: Pipeline Stages:
docs.text:
1. Ingestion (Layer 1): Load documents from 82+ sources
  2. Chunking (Layer 2): Split documents into manageable pieces
  3. Embedding (Layer 3): Convert text to numerical vectors
  4. Vector Store (Layer 4): Index and store embeddings
  5. Retrieval (Layer 5): Find relevant chunks for a query
  6. Reranking (Layer 6): Refine retrieval results
  7. Generation (Layer 7): Generate answers with LLMs

docs.title: 2.1 Layer Independence
docs.text:
RAGBench's core principle is layer independence. Each layer:

  • Imports nothing from other layers (except data models)
  • Works standalone with its own API
  • Has no side effects on other layers
  • Is fully tested in isolation

docs.title: 2.1.1 Enforcement
docs.text:
Layer independence is enforced by:

  1. Import checks: tests/test_independence.py fails if layers import each other
  2. Integration tests: Each layer has standalone tests
  3. Type contracts: Layers communicate through small, typed interfaces

docs.title: 2.1.2 Benefits
docs.text:
• Flexibility: Use only the layers you need
  • Maintainability: Changes don't cascade
  • Testing: Mock dependencies easily
  • Understanding: Learn one layer at a time

docs.title: 2.2 Data Contracts
docs.text: Layers communicate through simple data structures:

docs.title: Document (Layer 1 → 2)
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Document:
    id: str                    # Unique identifier
    content: str              # Text content
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]  # Source, page, etc.
    modality: str             # text, image, audio, etc.

docs.title: Chunk (Layer 2 → 3)
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Chunk:
    id: str                    # Unique identifier
    document_id: str          # Parent document
    content: str              # Chunk text
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]  # Position, method, etc.

docs.title: EmbeddedChunk (Layer 3 → 4)
docs.text:
@dataclass
class EmbeddedChunk:
    id: str                    # Unique identifier
    chunk_id: str             # Parent chunk
    document_id: str          # Root document
    content: str              # Text content
    vector: List[float]       # Dense embedding
    sparse: Dict[int, float]  # Sparse embedding
    multi_vector: List[List[float]]  # Multi-vector
    model: str                # Embedding model
    dim: int                  # Vector dimension
    modality: str             # text, image, etc.
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]

docs.title: RetrievalResult (Layer 5 → 6)
docs.text:
@dataclass
class RetrievalResult:
    id: str                    # Unique identifier
    score: float              # Relevance (higher = better)
    content: str              # Retrieved text
    chunk_id: str             # Source chunk
    document_id: str          # Source document
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]  # Additional info

docs.title: GeneratedAnswer (Layer 7)
docs.text:
@dataclass
class GeneratedAnswer:
    answer: str               # Generated text
    citations: List[Citation] # Source citations
    query: str                # Original query
    model: str                # LLM model used
    tokens_used: int          # Token count
    duration_s: float         # Generation time

docs.title: 2.4 Registry Pattern
docs.text:
Every layer uses the Registry Pattern for method discovery:

# Embedding registry
from ragbench.embedding import REGISTRY

# List all methods
methods = REGISTRY.list_names()  # 61 methods

# Get method info
info = REGISTRY.get("openai")

# List by category
api_methods = REGISTRY.list_by_category("api")

# Check availability
status = REGISTRY.status("bge")  # available, unavailable, missing_packages

Benefits: - Auto-discovery: New methods are automatically found - Lazy loading: Heavy imports only when used - Status checking: Know what's available - Metadata: Query capabilities without loading

docs.title: 2.5 Routing System
docs.text: RAGBench's auto-routing intelligently selects methods:

docs.title: 2.5.1 Embedding Routing
docs.text:
# Explicit method
embed(text, method="openai")  # Use OpenAI

# Auto-routing (checks in order):
# 1. Explicit method parameter
# 2. Language hint in metadata
# 3. Modality (text, image, code, etc.)
# 4. Configured default (OMNILOAD_EMBEDDER)
# 5. hash_baseline (offline fallback)
embed(text, method="auto")

docs.title: 2.5.2 Retrieval Routing
docs.text:
# Auto-routing considers:
# - Query type (keyword, question, code, etc.)
# - Store capabilities (dense, sparse, hybrid)
# - Filters (metadata conditions)
# - Collection count (single vs multi)

retrieve(query, method="auto", store=my_store)

docs.title: 2.5.3 Chunking Routing
docs.text:
# Routes based on:
# - File extension
# - Content type
# - Document structure
# - Explicit method parameter

chunk(document, method="auto")

docs.title: 2.6 Error Handling
docs.text:
RAGBench has a comprehensive error hierarchy:

# Base errors
RAGBenchError                 # All errors inherit from this

# Layer-specific errors
EmbeddingError
  ├─ MissingCredentialError   # API key missing
  ├─ DependencyMissingError   # Package not installed
  ├─ ModelNotFoundError       # Model doesn't exist
  └─ QuotaExceededError       # Rate limit hit

GenerationError
  ├─ ConfigError              # Invalid configuration
  ├─ ProviderError            # API/provider error
  ├─ TransientError           # Temporary (retry)
  ├─ ContextLengthError       # Input too long
  └─ RefusalError             # Model refused (safety)

RetrievalError
VectorStoreError

docs.title: 4.3 Complete Example: Local Setup (No API Keys)
docs.text:
This example uses only free, local tools:

from ragbench.pipeline import ask, auto

# === INDEXING PHASE ===

documents = [
    "Quantum computing uses qubits that can be in superposition.",
    "Classical computers use bits that are either 0 or 1.",
    "Quantum entanglement allows qubits to be correlated.",
    "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence.",
    "Neural networks are inspired by biological neurons."
]

print("Indexing documents...")
for i, doc in enumerate(documents):
    auto(
        doc,
        as_text=True,
        embed=True,
        embedder="hash_baseline",  # Free, offline
        index=True,
        store="memory",  # In-memory, no setup
        collection="tech_docs"
    )
    print(f"  ✓ Indexed {i+1}/{len(documents)}")

# === QUERYING PHASE ===

print("\nAsking questions...")

# Question 1
answer1 = ask(
    query="What is quantum computing?",
    collection="tech_docs",
    store="memory",
    embedder="hash_baseline",
    k=3,  # Retrieve top 3 chunks
    rerank=True,
    rerank_method="bm25",  # Free, offline
    rerank_k=2,  # Keep top 2 after reranking
    generation_method="ollama",  # Free, local
    generation_options={"model": "llama3.1"}
)

print(f"\nQ: What is quantum computing?")
print(f"A: {answer1.answer}\n")

# Question 2
answer2 = ask(
    query="Explain machine learning",
    collection="tech_docs",
    store="memory",
    embedder="hash_baseline",
    generation_method="ollama"
)

print(f"Q: Explain machine learning")
print(f"A: {answer2.answer}\n")

docs.title: 4.4 Complete Example: Cloud Setup (With API Keys)
docs.text:
This example uses cloud APIs for better quality:

import os
from ragbench.pipeline import ask, auto

# Set API keys
os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "sk-..."
os.environ["COHERE_API_KEY"] = "..."

# === INDEXING ===

print("Indexing with OpenAI embeddings...")
result = auto(
    "path/to/documents/",  # Directory of files
    embed=True,
    embedder="openai",  # High-quality embeddings
    embed_options={"model": "text-embedding-3-small"},
    index=True,
    store="sqlite",  # Persistent local storage
    collection="company_docs"
)

print(f"✓ Indexed {len(result.ids)} chunks")

# === QUERYING ===

print("\nQuerying with full RAG pipeline...")
answer = ask(
    query="What are our Q4 revenue projections?",
    collection="company_docs",
    store="sqlite",
    embedder="openai",
    k=20,  # Retrieve more chunks
    rerank=True,
    rerank_method="cohere",  # Best reranker
    rerank_k=5,  # Keep top 5
    generation_method="openai",  # GPT-4
    generation_options={
        "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
        "temperature": 0.3  # More factual
    },
    include_retrieval=True,  # Return retrieval results
    include_reranking=True   # Return reranking results
)

print(f"\n{'='*70}")
print(f"Query: {answer['answer'].query}")
print(f"{'='*70}")
print(f"\nAnswer:\n{answer['answer'].answer}")
print(f"\nMetadata:")
print(f"  • Retrieved: {len(answer.get('retrieval', []))} chunks")
print(f"  • Reranked to: {len(answer.get('reranking', []))} chunks")
print(f"  • Model: {answer['answer'].model}")
print(f"  • Tokens: {answer['answer'].tokens_used}")
print(f"  • Duration: {answer['answer'].duration_s:.2f}s")
print(f"  • Citations: {len(answer['answer'].citations)}")

if answer['answer'].citations:
    print(f"\nSources:")
    for i, citation in enumerate(answer['answer'].citations, 1):
        print(f"  [{i}] {citation.document_id}")
        print(f"      Score: {citation.score:.2f}")
        print(f"      Content: {citation.content[:100]}...")

docs.title: 4.5 Streaming Responses
docs.text:
For better user experience, stream tokens as they're generated:

from ragbench.pipeline import ask

print("Answer: ", end="", flush=True)

# Stream tokens in real-time
for token in ask(
    query="Explain quantum entanglement",
    collection="tech_docs",
    store="memory",
    embedder="hash_baseline",
    generation_method="ollama",
    streaming=True  # Enable streaming
):
    print(token, end="", flush=True)

print()  # Newline

docs.title: 4.6 Multi-Turn Conversations
docs.text:
Build chatbots with conversation history:

from ragbench.pipeline import ask
from ragbench.generation import Conversation

# Create conversation
conversation = Conversation()

# Turn 1
print("User: What is supervised learning?")
answer1 = ask(
    query="What is supervised learning?",
    collection="ml_docs",
    generation_method="ollama",
    conversation=conversation
)
print(f"Assistant: {answer1.answer}\n")

# Add to history
conversation.add_user("What is supervised learning?")
conversation.add_assistant(answer1.answer)

# Turn 2 (context-aware)
print("User: How does it differ from unsupervised learning?")
answer2 = ask(
    query="How does it differ from unsupervised learning?",
    collection="ml_docs",
    generation_method="ollama",
    conversation=conversation  # Pass history
)
print(f"Assistant: {answer2.answer}\n")

# Turn 3
conversation.add_user("How does it differ from unsupervised learning?")
conversation.add_assistant(answer2.answer)

print("User: Give me an example")
answer3 = ask(
    query="Give me an example",
    collection="ml_docs",
    generation_method="ollama",
    conversation=conversation
)
print(f"Assistant: {answer3.answer}\n")

docs.title: 5.1 Overview
docs.text: The ingestion layer loads documents from 82+ data sources into RAGBench's canonical Document format.

docs.title: 5.1.1 Key Features
docs.text:
• 82 Connectors: PDF, Office, databases, APIs, cloud storage, etc.
  • Format Preservation: Retains structure (tables, images, metadata)
  • Error Handling: Robust parsing with fallbacks
  • Metadata Extraction: Author, date, page numbers, etc.

docs.title: 5.1.2 Document Format
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Document:
    id: str                    # Unique identifier
    content: str              # Text content
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]  # Source metadata
    modality: str             # text, image, audio, video, etc.
    language: Optional[str]   # Detected language
    embedding: Optional[List[float]]  # Pre-computed embedding

docs.title: 6.1.1 Why Chunking?
docs.text:
• Embedding Limits: Models have token limits (e.g., 8192 tokens)
  • Retrieval Precision: Smaller chunks = more relevant results
  • Context Windows: LLMs work better with focused context
  • Performance: Faster search over smaller units

  • Fixed: Character, token, sentence count
  • Semantic: Meaning-based boundaries

  • Structure-aware: Markdown, HTML, JSON, code
  • Adaptive: Dynamic sizing based on content

docs.text:
General guidelines: - Small chunks (100-300 chars): High precision, more chunks, slower - Medium chunks (500-1000 chars): Balanced, recommended for most cases - Large chunks (1000-2000 chars): More context, fewer chunks, faster

By use case: - Q&A: 500-800 characters - Summarization: 1000-2000 characters - Code search: Function-level (varies) - Long documents: Hierarchical (parent: 2000, child: 500)

docs.title: 7.1 Overview
docs.text: The embedding layer converts text into numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning.

docs.title: 7.1.1 What are Embeddings?
docs.text:
Embeddings are dense vector representations of text where: - Similar meanings → Similar vectors - Semantic relationships preserved - Enables vector similarity search

Example: 

"cat"     → [0.2, 0.8, 0.1, ...]
"kitten"  → [0.3, 0.7, 0.2, ...]  # Close to "cat"
"dog"     → [0.4, 0.6, 0.3, ...]  # Somewhat close
"car"     → [0.9, 0.1, 0.8, ...]  # Far from "cat"

docs.title: 7.1.2 Why Embeddings?
docs.text:
• Semantic Search: Find meaning, not just keywords
  • Similarity: Measure relatedness between texts
  • Clustering: Group similar documents
  • Classification: Category prediction
  • Recommendation: Find related content

docs.title: 7.1.3 Embedding Types
docs.text: RAGBench supports: - Dense: Single vector per text (most common) - Sparse: Keyword-based (BM25, TF-IDF) - Multi-vector: Multiple vectors per text (ColBERT) - Hybrid: Combination of dense + sparse

def normalize_dims(vectors, target_dim):
    from numpy import zeros
    normalized = []
    for vec in vectors:
        if len(vec) < target_dim:
            padded = zeros(target_dim)
            padded[:len(vec)] = vec
            normalized.append(padded)
        else:
            normalized.append(vec[:target_dim])

docs.title: 8.1 Overview
docs.text: The vector store layer indexes and retrieves embeddings efficiently.

docs.title: 8.1.1 What is a Vector Store?
docs.text: A vector store (vector database) is specialized storage for: - High-dimensional vectors (embeddings) - Similarity search (find nearest neighbors) - Metadata filtering (search with conditions) - Scalability (billions of vectors)

docs.title: 8.1.2 Why Vector Stores?
docs.text: Compared to traditional databases: - ✅ Fast similarity search: O(log n) vs O(n) - ✅ Optimized for vectors: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbors) - ✅ Metadata filters: Combined vector + attribute search - ✅ Scalability: Distributed, sharded storage

docs.title: 8.1.3 Available Stores (41 total)
docs.text: RAGBench supports: - Local: Memory, SQLite, DuckDB, FAISS, ChromaDB - Cloud: Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus - Databases: PostgreSQL (pgvector), Redis, MongoDB - Search engines: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch

docs.text: The retrieval layer finds the most relevant chunks for a given query.

docs.title: 9.1.1 Retrieval Methods (28 total)
docs.text:
RAGBench provides diverse retrieval strategies:

  • Dense: Vector similarity search
  • Sparse: Keyword matching (BM25, TF-IDF)
  • Hybrid: Combined dense + sparse
  • Fusion: Merge multiple retrieval results
  • Diversity: MMR, max-sum diversification
  • Query Transforms: Rewrite, HyDE, multi-query
  • Expansion: Parent-child, sentence window
  • Routing: Auto-select best method

docs.text: Reranking refines retrieval results by reordering them based on deeper relevance analysis.

docs.title: 10.1.1 Why Rerank?
docs.text: Initial retrieval (Layer 5) is fast but may not be perfect. Reranking: - ✅ Improves precision: Better ranking of top results - ✅ Cross-encoder models: More accurate than bi-encoders - ✅ Domain-specific: Use specialized models - ✅ Hybrid signals: Combine multiple relevance indicators

  • API-based: Cohere, Voyage, Jina
  • Learning-to-rank: LambdaMART, RankNet
  • Diversity: MMR reranking
  • Custom: Rule-based, ML models

@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)
def cached_ask(query_hash, collection):

import numpy as np

def maxsim_score(query_vecs, doc_vecs):
    """
    MaxSim: For each query vector, find max similarity with doc vectors.
    Sum these max similarities.
    """
    scores = []

    for q_vec in query_vecs:
        # Compute similarity with all doc vectors
        sims = [np.dot(q_vec, d_vec) for d_vec in doc_vecs]
        # Take max
        scores.append(max(sims))

    # Sum maxs
    return sum(scores)

    elif query_lower.startswith(('explain', 'why')):

def optimize_context(results, max_tokens=4000):
    """Fit results into context window."""

    # Estimate tokens (rough: 1 token ≈ 4 chars)
    def estimate_tokens(text):
        return len(text) // 4

    selected = []
    total_tokens = 0

    for r in results:
        chunk_tokens = estimate_tokens(r.content)

        if total_tokens + chunk_tokens <= max_tokens:
            selected.append(r)
            total_tokens += chunk_tokens
        else:
            # Truncate if space remains
            remaining = max_tokens - total_tokens
            if remaining > 50:  # Minimum useful size
                truncated = r.content[:remaining * 4]
                r.content = truncated
                selected.append(r)
            break

    return selected

# Use optimized context

optimized = optimize_context(results, max_tokens=3000)

from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
import numpy as np

class LTRReranker:
    """Learning to Rank reranker."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.model = GradientBoostingClassifier()
        self.is_trained = False

    def extract_features(self, query, result):
        """Extract features for ranking."""

        features = [
            result.score,  # Original score
            len(result.content),  # Length
            result.content.lower().count(query.lower()),  # Query frequency
            result.metadata.get("year", 2000),  # Recency
            result.metadata.get("citations", 0),  # Citations
            1 if result.metadata.get("source_type") == "official" else 0,  # Authority
        ]

        return features

    def train(self, queries, results_list, labels):
        """Train on labeled data."""

        X = []
        y = []

        for query, results, relevance_labels in zip(queries, results_list, labels):
            for result, label in zip(results, relevance_labels):
                features = self.extract_features(query, result)
                X.append(features)
                y.append(label)

        self.model.fit(X, y)
        self.is_trained = True

    def rerank(self, query, results):
        """Rerank results."""

        if not self.is_trained:
            raise ValueError("Model not trained")

        # Extract features
        X = [self.extract_features(query, r) for r in results]

        # Predict scores
        scores = self.model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]

        # Update scores
        for r, score in zip(results, scores):
            r.score = score

        # Sort
        results.sort(key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)

        return results

# Train
ltr = LTRReranker()

def evaluate_retrieval(queries, ground_truth, retrieval_fn, k=10):
    """Evaluate retrieval quality."""

    metrics = {
        "precision": [],
        "recall": [],
        "f1": [],
        "mrr": [],  # Mean Reciprocal Rank
        "ndcg": []  # Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain
    }

    for query, relevant_ids in zip(queries, ground_truth):
        # Retrieve
        results = retrieval_fn(query, k=k)
        retrieved_ids = [r.id for r in results]

        # Precision: % retrieved that are relevant
        relevant_retrieved = set(retrieved_ids) & set(relevant_ids)
        precision = len(relevant_retrieved) / len(retrieved_ids)

        # Recall: % relevant that are retrieved
        recall = len(relevant_retrieved) / len(relevant_ids)

        # F1
        if precision + recall > 0:
            f1 = 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall)
        else:
            f1 = 0

        # MRR: 1 / rank of first relevant
        mrr = 0
        for i, rid in enumerate(retrieved_ids, 1):
            if rid in relevant_ids:
                mrr = 1 / i
                break

        # NDCG (simplified)
        # ... (complex calculation)

        metrics["precision"].append(precision)
        metrics["recall"].append(recall)
        metrics["f1"].append(f1)
        metrics["mrr"].append(mrr)

    # Average
    return {
        "avg_precision": np.mean(metrics["precision"]),
        "avg_recall": np.mean(metrics["recall"]),
        "avg_f1": np.mean(metrics["f1"]),
        "avg_mrr": np.mean(metrics["mrr"])
    }

from ragbench.generation import Generator

def evaluate_generation(queries, ground_truth_answers, context_fn, generator):
    """Evaluate generation quality."""

    # Simple metrics
    from difflib import SequenceMatcher

    similarities = []

    for query, true_answer in zip(queries, ground_truth_answers):
        # Get context
        context = context_fn(query)

        # Generate answer
        generated = generator.generate(query, context)

        # Compare with ground truth
        similarity = SequenceMatcher(
            None, 
            generated.answer.lower(), 
            true_answer.lower()
        ).ratio()

        similarities.append(similarity)

    return {
        "avg_similarity": np.mean(similarities),
        "min_similarity": np.min(similarities),
        "max_similarity": np.max(similarities)
    }

# Better: Use LLM-based evaluation
def llm_evaluate(generated_answer, true_answer, evaluator_llm):
    """Use LLM to evaluate answer quality."""

    prompt = f"""Rate the quality of this generated answer on a scale of 1-5:

    Question: {query}
    Expected Answer: {true_answer}
    Generated Answer: {generated_answer}

    Consider:
    - Accuracy
    - Completeness
    - Relevance

    Output only the number (1-5):"""

    score = evaluator_llm.generate_text(prompt)
    return int(score.strip())

def enrich_metadata(document):
    """Add useful metadata."""

    metadata = document.metadata.copy()

    # Extract date
    date_match = re.search(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', document.content)
    if date_match:
        metadata["date"] = date_match.group()

    # Detect language
    from langdetect import detect
    metadata["language"] = detect(document.content[:1000])

    # Calculate statistics
    metadata["word_count"] = len(document.content.split())
    metadata["char_count"] = len(document.content)

    # Add source type

        metadata["source_type"] = "pdf"

    document.metadata = metadata

import hashlib

def deduplicate_chunks(chunks):
    """Remove duplicate chunks."""

    seen = set()
    unique = []

    for c in chunks:
        # Hash content
        content_hash = hashlib.md5(c.content.encode()).hexdigest()

        if content_hash not in seen:
            seen.add(content_hash)
            unique.append(c)

    print(f"Removed {len(chunks) - len(unique)} duplicates")
    return unique

    """Choose chunking method based on content."""

    content = document.content

    # Code
    if any(ext in document.metadata.get("source", "") 
           for ext in [".py", ".js", ".java"]):
        return chunk(content, method="Code Chunking")

    # Markdown
    elif content.startswith("#") or "##" in content:
        return chunk(content, method="Markdown Chunking")

    # JSON/YAML
    elif content.strip().startswith(("{", "[")):
        return chunk(content, method="JSON Chunking")

    # HTML
    elif "<html" in content.lower():
        return chunk(content, method="HTML Chunking")

    # Long form
    elif len(content) > 10000:
        return chunk(content, method="Hierarchical Chunking")

    # Default
    else:
        return chunk(content, method="Recursive Character Chunking")

        self.queries = []

def robust_ask(query, collection):
    """Ask with fallbacks."""

    # Try primary configuration
    try:
        return ask(
            query,
            collection=collection,
            embedder="openai",
            generation_method="openai"
        )

    # Fallback 1: Local embedder
    except EmbeddingError:
        logger.warning("OpenAI embedder failed, using local")
        try:
            return ask(
                query,
                collection=collection,
                embedder="bge",
                generation_method="openai"
            )
        except:
            pass

    # Fallback 2: Local LLM
    except GenerationError:
        logger.warning("OpenAI generation failed, using Ollama")
        return ask(
            query,
            collection=collection,
            embedder="openai",
            generation_method="ollama"
        )

    # Fallback 3: All local
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"All primary methods failed: {e}")
        return ask(
            query,
            collection=collection,
            embedder="hash_baseline",
            generation_method="ollama"

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

class RateLimiter:
    """Simple rate limiter."""

    def __init__(self, max_requests=10, window_seconds=60):
        self.max_requests = max_requests
        self.window = timedelta(seconds=window_seconds)
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def allow(self, user_id):
        """Check if request is allowed."""
        now = datetime.now()

        # Clean old requests
        self.requests[user_id] = [
            req_time for req_time in self.requests[user_id]
            if now - req_time < self.window
        ]

        # Check limit
        if len(self.requests[user_id]) >= self.max_requests:
            return False

        # Record request
        self.requests[user_id].append(now)
        return True

# Usage
limiter = RateLimiter(max_requests=10, window_seconds=60)

if limiter.allow(user_id):
    answer = ask(query, collection="docs")
else:
    print("Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.")

        **config
    ):
        """Initialize retriever."""

    def retrieve(
        self,
        query: str,
        collection: str,
        k: int = 10,
        filter: Optional[Dict] = None,
        **kwargs
    ) -> List[RetrievalResult]:
        """Retrieve results."""

    def retrieve_report(
        self,
        query: str,
        collection: str,
        k: int = 10,
        **kwargs
    ) -> RetrievalReport:
        """Retrieve with detailed report."""

docs.title: 19.3.4 Generation
docs.text:
class Generator:
    def __init__(self, method: str, **config):
        """Initialize generator."""

    def generate(
        self,
        query: str,
        context: List[Dict],
        conversation: Optional[Conversation] = None,
        template: Optional[PromptTemplate] = None,
        **kwargs
    ) -> GeneratedAnswer:
        """Generate answer."""

    def generate_stream(
        self,
        query: str,
        context: List[Dict],
        **kwargs
    ) -> Iterator[str]:
        """Generate streaming answer."""

    def is_available(self) -> bool:
        """Check if generator is available."""

docs.title: 20.1 Glossary
docs.text:
RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation - technique combining retrieval and generation

Embedding: Numerical vector representation of text

Dense Vector: Fixed-length continuous vector (e.g., [0.2, 0.8, 0.1, ...])

Sparse Vector: Dictionary of term → weight (e.g., {125: 0.45, 389: 0.82})

Multi-Vector: Multiple vectors per text (e.g., ColBERT)

Chunk: Small piece of document for processing

Collection: Named group of vectors in a store

Namespace: Logical partition within a collection

Reranking: Refining retrieval results with deeper analysis

Cross-Encoder: Model that scores query-document pairs directly

Bi-Encoder: Separate encoders for queries and documents

Late Interaction: Computing fine-grained similarity (e.g., ColBERT)

MMR: Maximal Marginal Relevance - diversification algorithm

HyDE: Hypothetical Document Embeddings

RRF: Reciprocal Rank Fusion

ANN: Approximate Nearest Neighbors

HNSW: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph

IVF: Inverted File index

PQ: Product Quantization

docs.title: 1.1 Absolute Minimum (No API Keys, Offline)
docs.text:
This gets you started with zero external dependencies:

# Python 3.9 or higher
python --version  # Should be 3.9+

# Install base package
pip install ragbench-ai

# That's it! You can now use:
# - hash_baseline embedder (offline, non-semantic)
# - BM25 retrieval (offline)
# - Memory/SQLite vector store (local)
# - Ollama LLM (requires separate install)

What you can do: - ✅ Ingest documents (82 connectors) - ✅ Chunk text (106 methods) - ✅ Basic embedding (hash_baseline) - ✅ Store vectors locally - ✅ Keyword search (BM25) - ⚠️ No semantic search (use API or install local models) - ⚠️ No LLM generation (need Ollama or API)

docs.text:

pip install "ragbench-ai[embed-local,generate-ollama]"

# 2. Install Ollama (local LLM)
# macOS/Linux:
curl -fsSL https://ollama.ai/install.sh | sh

# Windows: Download from https://ollama.ai

# 3. Pull a model
ollama pull llama3.1

# 4. Start Ollama
ollama serve

# Now you have a complete local RAG system!

What you can do: - ✅ Everything from minimal + - ✅ Semantic embeddings (BGE, E5, etc.) - ✅ Local LLM generation (Llama 3.1, Mistral, etc.) - ✅ Complete RAG pipeline offline - ✅ No API costs

# test_installation.py

import sys

def test_ragbench():
    """Test RAGBench installation."""
    print("Testing RAGBench installation...")

    try:
        import ragbench
        print(f"✓ RAGBench version: {ragbench.__version__}")
    except ImportError as e:
        print(f"✗ RAGBench not installed: {e}")
        return False

    return True

def test_embedders():
    """Test available embedders."""
    print("\nTesting embedders...")

    try:
        from ragbench.embedding import REGISTRY

        embedders = REGISTRY.list_names()
        print(f"✓ Found {len(embedders)} embedders")

        # Test hash_baseline (always available)
        from ragbench.embedding import Embedder
        embedder = Embedder("hash_baseline")
        vec = embedder.embed(["test"])[0]
        print(f"✓ Hash baseline works: {len(vec.vector)} dimensions")

        # Test local embedders if available
        try:
            embedder = Embedder("bge")
            if embedder.is_available():
                print("✓ Local embedders (BGE) available")
            else:
                print("⚠ Local embedders not available (install with [embed-local])")
        except:
            print("⚠ Local embedders not installed")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Embedder test failed: {e}")
        return False

    return True

def test_vector_stores():
    """Test available vector stores."""
    print("\nTesting vector stores...")

    try:
        from ragbench.vectorstore import VectorStore

        # Test memory store (always available)
        store = VectorStore("memory")
        print("✓ Memory store available")

        # Test SQLite
        try:
            store = VectorStore("sqlite", path=":memory:")
            print("✓ SQLite store available")
        except:
            print("⚠ SQLite store not available")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Vector store test failed: {e}")
        return False

    return True

def test_generation():
    """Test generation layer."""
    print("\nTesting generation...")

    try:
        from ragbench.generation import Generator

        # Test Ollama
        try:
            gen = Generator(method="ollama")
            if gen.is_available():
                print("✓ Ollama available")
            else:
                print("⚠ Ollama not running (start with 'ollama serve')")
        except:
            print("⚠ Ollama not installed")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Generation test failed: {e}")
        return False

    return True

def test_pipeline():
    """Test pipeline functions."""
    print("\nTesting pipeline...")

    try:
        from ragbench.pipeline import auto, ask

        # Test chunking
        chunks = auto("Hello world test", as_text=True)
        print(f"✓ Pipeline auto() works: {len(chunks)} chunks")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Pipeline test failed: {e}")
        return False

    return True

def main():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("RAGBench Installation Verification")
    print("=" * 60)

    results = []
    results.append(("RAGBench", test_ragbench()))
    results.append(("Embedders", test_embedders()))
    results.append(("Vector Stores", test_vector_stores()))
    results.append(("Generation", test_generation()))
    results.append(("Pipeline", test_pipeline()))

    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("Summary:")
    print("=" * 60)

    for name, passed in results:
        status = "✓ PASS" if passed else "✗ FAIL"
        print(f"{name}: {status}")

    all_passed = all(r[1] for r in results)

    if all_passed:
        print("\n✓ All tests passed! RAGBench is ready to use.")
    else:
        print("\n⚠ Some tests failed. Check output above for details.")

    return 0 if all_passed else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Run verification:

python test_installation.py

# check_resources.py

import psutil
import torch

def check_resources():
    print("System Resources:")
    print("=" * 50)

    # CPU
    cpu_count = psutil.cpu_count()
    cpu_percent = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1)
    print(f"CPU: {cpu_count} cores, {cpu_percent}% used")

    # RAM
    ram = psutil.virtual_memory()
    print(f"RAM: {ram.total / (1024**3):.1f} GB total, {ram.percent}% used")

    # Disk
    disk = psutil.disk_usage('/')
    print(f"Disk: {disk.total / (1024**3):.1f} GB total, {disk.percent}% used")

    # GPU
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        print(f"\nGPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
        print(f"CUDA version: {torch.version.cuda}")
        print(f"GPU memory: {torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / (1024**3):.1f} GB")
    else:
        print("\nGPU: Not available")

    # Apple Silicon
    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        print("\nApple Silicon (MPS): Available")

    print("\nRecommendations:")
    if ram.total < 8 * (1024**3):
        print("⚠ Consider using API-based embeddings (low RAM)")
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        print("ℹ GPU not available - using CPU (slower for local models)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    check_resources()
